look_here_first: Spring-fruiting prairie sedge with 2–4 distinct rounded spikes and large flat silvery-white winged perigynia.

project_inclusion.range_basis: User has one wild iNaturalist observation; GRIN/ITIS/FNA accept Carex tetrastachya Scheele as native in Texas.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; exact target-zone county reconciliation is deferred and native metrics remain excluded.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Cyperaceae/Carex: grasslike sedges with sheathing leaves; the fruit is enclosed in a perigynium, and perigynium shape/beak/venation are often decisive for species ID.
best_field_traits: usually 2–4 distant ovoid to globose spikes
perigynia broad, flat and strongly winged
mesic to moist prairie, roadside ditch and shore habitat
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The broad flat white-winged perigynia are the giveaway. None of the other Carex in B105 has that papery silvery winged look.
